name: Statue of Liberty
heritage: World Heritage Site; Historic Civil Engineering Landmark; National Register of Historic Places contributing property; New York State Register of Historic Places listed place; National Register of Historic Places listed place; New York City Landmark
type: statue; part of UNESCO World Heritage Site; observation tower; colossal statue
text: The Statue of Liberty (Liberty Enlightening the World, French: La Liberté éclairant le monde) is a colossal neoclassical sculpture of a robed and crowned woman on Liberty Island, part of New York City, in New York Harbor. The copper-clad statue, a gift to the United States from the people of France, was designed by French sculptor Frédéric Auguste Bartholdi, and its metal framework built by Gustave Eiffel. The statue was dedicated on October 28, 1886.
